name: Merritt Bookkeeping
description: Merritt Bookkeeping provides human bookkeeping services, QuickBooks-based books, monthly financial reports, and a browser-based review workflow.
agentUseSummary: Merritt Bookkeeping cannot currently be connected as a Relay agent provider because it publishes no supported public customer API, delegated OAuth contract, customer API key, remote MCP service, webhook schema, or distributable operation contract. Merritt collects bank statements, maintains a separate QuickBooks bookkeeping file, and sends reports for review through its own web interface; those service workflows do not grant Relay authority. Relay will not reuse portal sessions, capture banking credentials, automate the review interface, or infer private endpoints.

blocked.label: Connect Merritt Bookkeeping
blocked.description: Merritt Bookkeeping publishes no supported public OAuth, customer API key, remote MCP, webhook, or other delegated account contract for Relay to implement.

blocked.label: Access bookkeeping or financial data
blocked.description: Bank and card statements, transactions, categories, QuickBooks files, spreadsheets, reports, forecasts, margins, messages, documents, and customer information are blocked without a supported authenticated API.

blocked.label: Perform bookkeeping or account actions
blocked.description: Statement collection, transaction entry or editing, categorization, reconciliation, report review, change requests, file access, messages, exports, account changes, and all other writes or submissions are blocked.

blocked.label: Use unsupported automation
blocked.description: Relay will not automate Merritt's review interface, reuse browser sessions, capture Merritt, bank, or QuickBooks credentials, access invitation or report links, scrape spreadsheets, reverse-engineer private endpoints, or treat Merritt's access to bank statements or QuickBooks as Relay authority.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled without a supported customer-authenticated Merritt Bookkeeping API or remote MCP contract with stable schemas and least-privilege authorization.

runtimeSupport.description: No customer-authenticated Merritt Bookkeeping operation is available to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No customer-authenticated Merritt Bookkeeping operation is available to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Merritt documents a human bookkeeping service that collects bank statements, maintains customer books in a separate QuickBooks file, emails monthly reports, and accepts review changes through a custom browser interface. It publishes no Merritt customer API, OAuth application contract, customer token, remote MCP service, webhook schema, stable operation schemas, sandbox, scopes, or revocation contract for independent third-party automation.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not expose Connect, request Merritt, bank, or QuickBooks credentials, publish runtime tools, access report links, or automate the review interface. Reconsider only if Merritt publishes a supported customer-authenticated API or remote MCP service with stable schemas, least-privilege read scopes, revocation, audit semantics, financial-data controls, and human confirmation for bookkeeping, account, and financial actions.

evidence.supports: Merritt states that automated software collects bank statements, human bookkeepers work in QuickBooks, and customers review reports in a custom web interface. It does not document a public Merritt API or delegated authentication contract.

Merritt maintains a separate QuickBooks bookkeeping file, exports transactions to a spreadsheet for customer review, and applies requested edits itself. Third-party QuickBooks connections are not copied into that file and do not grant Relay a Merritt operation surface.

Merritt describes itself as a service powered by real humans rather than software, with emailed reports, QuickBooks-based books, a review interface, and accountant collaboration. No API credentials, scopes, webhooks, or developer documentation are offered.

Merritt's terms prohibit making the service available to others, unauthorized access, reverse engineering, decompilation, hacking, and disruption. The terms do not establish an API or delegated Relay authorization path.
